subject: Competitive bake-off recap
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Taylor Nguyen <taylor@orchid-labs.com>, Chris Patel <chris.p@orchid-labs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Competitive bake-off recap 

Hi Taylor / Chris 

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we keep momentum for the proof-of-concept (POC) bake-off. I captured the pain, your goals, the decision criteria you agreed on, and outstanding questions. Please reply with any corrections.

Summary of pain & goals
- Pain: Current AI infra is inconsistent across teams; slow tail latency at 95th pct due to synchronous batching and lack of prefix cache. Hard to get predictable cost at scale.
- Goal: Replace the inference layer for customer-facing features to achieve: sub-150ms median single-request latency, predictable per-token cost, and ability to run private deployments in VPC for regulated datasets.

Decision criteria (what matters for Orchid)
1) Latency & tail behavior (95/99pct) under production mix
2) Cost per 1M tokens + ability to control batch sizing/quantization
3) Data security: VPC + KMS support and audit logs
4) Developer ergonomics: API parity and rollout tooling (canary/A-B)
5) Support model variants and fallbacks if capacity constrained

Competitive context discussed
- Competitor A: good latency but limited private deploy options
- Competitor B: cheaper at scale but inconsistent latency under bursty traffic
- Redwood: unified runtime, prefix caching and routing policies that map to your requirements (we'll demonstrate).

Open questions / unknowns (we'll address these in the bake-off)
- Can we reproduce your 95th-pct latency on your traffic trace (you agreed to share a sanitized trace)?
- Which models do you want to include? You suggested: MPT-30B-q4, LLaMA-2-13B, and llm-open-1.
- Any strict SLA requirements for commit dates?

Proposed bake-off plan (attached: MVP_bakeoff_plan.xlsx)
- Week 0: Exchange sanitized trace + dataset definitions (Orchid)
- Week 1: Baseline runs across 3 vendors on Orchid traffic (Redwood will run on Dedicated and Private where possible)
- Week 2: Tail-latency stress tests + cost modeling report
- Week 3: Joint review and decision matrix + next steps for pilot

Next steps / actions
- Taylor: share sanitized production trace and model list by Wed 3/24
- Chris: confirm whether Orchid needs on-prem (air-gapped) option or VPC-only
- Aditya / Marissa / Rishi: set up benchmark harness and share run instructions (drive link attached)
- Schedule 60m run kickoff: https://calendly.com/aditya-rao/redwood-bakeoff-run

Attachments: MVP_bakeoff_plan.xlsx, redwood-vs-other-comparison.pdf

Thanks 

Best,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

Subject: Re: Competitive bake-off recap 

Hi Aditya 

Thanks for the thorough write-up. A couple clarifications from our side: 
- Security: we'll provide a hashed/sanitized trace via secure share by Wed EOD; our infosec requires KMS-backed key management for logs retained beyond 30 days.
- Models: we want to include both open-source and managed variants  


- Cost model: can you give a high-level estimate for both Dedicated (reserved) and Private (VPC) modes? We mostly care about $/1M tokens at our 2M token/month projection.

Open question: do you support running the benchmark harness inside our VPC (preferred) or will we need to share traces externally?

I'll send the hashed trace and confirm dates once infra greenlights the share.

Thanks,
Taylor
VP Product, Orchid Labs

Thanks Taylor 

Answers / clarifications
- We can run the benchmark harness inside your VPC using an agentized runner and a short-lived IAM role 

- High-level cost estimates (very rough for scoping):
  - Dedicated (reserved pool): ~$180 / 1M tokens for LLaMA-2-13B equivalent profile
  - Private (VPC, customer-managed infra via our private control plane): ~$220 / 1M tokens (includes data plane management and longer retention SLAs)

Action log updated

- Chris: confirm on-prem vs VPC possibility (you noted VPC preferred)
- Marissa: lead benchmark runs (Marissa will own config and baseline)
